what_its_for: Oxiconazole nitrate is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal skin infections such as athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), and ringworm (tinea corporis). It works by killing the fungus that is causing your infection.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a cream or lotion that you apply directly to your skin. Wash and dry the affected area thoroughly before applying. Apply a thin layer of the cream or lotion to the infected skin and the area just around it. Gently rub it in. Wash your hands well after applying, unless you are treating your hands. Use this medicine only on your skin — do not put it in your eyes, mouth, or vagina.
dosing: Apply the cream or lotion to the affected area once or twice a day, as directed by your doctor. For athlete's foot, use it once daily at bedtime. For jock itch or ringworm, use it once or twice daily. Continue using it for the full length of time your doctor prescribed, even if your skin starts to look better. Stopping too early can allow the fungus to come back.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep the tube or bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze this medication. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the packaging.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If it accidentally gets into your eyes, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or plastic wrap unless your doctor tells you to, as this can increase side effects. Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or shoes while you have a fungal infection, as this can spread the infection to others.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if your skin infection does not improve after 2 to 4 weeks of treatment, or if it gets worse. Also call your doctor if you notice serious skin reactions such as severe redness, burning, blistering, swelling, or skin peeling in the treated area. If you develop signs of an allergic reaction — such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing — seek medical help right away.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. However, it is important to keep using this medicine for the full treatment period prescribed by your doctor. Athlete's foot is usually treated for 4 weeks. Jock itch and ringworm are usually treated for 2 weeks. Using it for the full time helps make sure the infection is completely gone and does not come back.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine, as its safety has not been fully established in these situations. This medicine is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years old unless specifically directed by a doctor. If you have sensitive skin or a history of skin allergies, let your doctor know before starting treatment.
